claims: Hip rotational capacity changes with hip position; {{canonicalName}} must name its body base and use a comfortable active path rather than a universal endpoint.

The standing supported and quadruped bases preserve the same controlled hip-circle task but change support, balance, and trunk constraints; record them as exact variants rather than silently merging delivery conditions.

Hip rotation is position-dependent and cannot be reduced to one muscle. Describe the hip rotator complex, gluteals, hip flexors, adductors, trunk stabilizers, and supporting limbs as task contributors rather than diagnostic findings.

A controlled hip circle combines flexion, abduction, external and internal rotation, extension, and adduction while the trunk and pelvis are managed according to the assigned base. Do not count compensatory lumbar or pelvic motion as hip range.
Support and body base alter task complexity and coordination demand. Difficulty fields describe the exercise task only, not participant skill or proficiency.

Technique-appropriate, progressively dosed movement requires monitoring of form and fatigue. Track sides, direction, support, range, cadence, symptoms, and compensation rather than assigning a universal recovery claim.
Use a stable surface, clear space, and stable support where assigned. Selection requires a safe base and communication of a stop rule, not an exercise-card participant classification.

No source establishes a universal dose for this exact drill. Use a conservative, quality-limited candidate dose and progress only when the assigned base, trunk, pelvis, and hip path remain repeatable.

Instructions must identify the exact base, support, leg, circle direction, quiet-trunk rule, range boundary, and reset. A completed repetition is one controlled circle in the assigned direction, not an uncontrolled leg swing.
Stop for sharp or increasing hip, groin, knee, back, wrist, shoulder, neurologic, balance, or other concerning symptoms; stop if the support, surface, or controlled path cannot be restored.

Use {{canonicalName}} only when the exact active hip-control task fits the session objective and downstream demands. Do not promise injury prevention, structural change, treatment, or automatic transfer.
Athlete support must show the exact assigned base, leg path, quiet-trunk boundary, comfortable range option, direction change, and stop signal.
Coach support should include an assigned-base check, front and side observation, support and floor check, side/direction log, compensation threshold, and escalation rule.

Accessibility must distinguish stable hand support, quadruped tolerance, optional padding, visual demonstration, plain-language cues, and stopping or substituting when the assigned base is inaccessible.

A standing base, quadruped base, stable hand support, range, tempo, and direction are explicit variant dimensions. A hip airplane, donkey kick, leg swing, or isolated rotation is a different primary task and must not be silently substituted.

YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com. Candidate media requires human review for exact variant, playback, safety, accessibility, captions, and demonstration quality before approval.

assessmentSummary.identity: Hip CARs are slow, active, unilateral controlled circles of the moving hip through a comfortable available range while the assigned base limits compensation. Standing with a stable hand support and quadruped are distinct support/base variants of the same hip-circle task; neither is a leg swing, hip airplane, donkey kick, or a diagnostic assessment.
currentCardFindings: Source 57 conflates standing and quadruped bases, leaving balance, upper-limb support, range, rep boundary, fatigue, substitutions, and media review unspecified.
Standing changes single-leg balance and support demand; quadruped changes hand/wrist/shoulder support and reduces balance demand. Both require separate exact variants.
Legacy low scores lack a task-only calibration basis; candidate values separate technical complexity from physical difficulty and remain human-calibration gated.

proposedDosage.progressWhen: both directions and sides remain controlled without compensation or symptoms at the assigned base

coachCues: Choose the assigned base before moving
Brace lightly and keep the pelvis as quiet as the task allows
Make one slow circle with the knee
Use a smaller circle before forcing range
athleteInstructions: Set up in the assigned standing-supported or quadruped position
Lift the moving knee without rushing
Draw a slow circle from the hip
Keep the rest of your body as still as you can
Return, reverse direction, and switch sides

calibrationEvidence.basis: hip rotation biomechanics, safe progressive-training guidance, legacy-card comparison, and metadata-only direct media candidates
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No trial establishes a unique Hip CAR difficulty score, dose, clinical outcome, or transfer effect for either exact base.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain one Hip CAR definition with standing stable-support and quadruped exact variants. Treat range, direction, tempo, and assigned support as delivery dimensions. Keep hip airplanes, leg swings, donkey kicks, isolated hip rotation, and diagnostic use as separate tasks or prohibited automatic substitutions.
